## So what is the composable unit?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Turn the question around. A `Distributions.jl` distribution is
  already an interface the whole of Julia understands, so write the
  epidemiology as distributions and the probabilistic programming
  language becomes optional rather than load bearing
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` does not depend on Turing. Nothing in
  `src/` mentions it, so nobody has to install a probabilistic
  programming language to get the distributions
- A composed delay comes back as a plain distribution type, and every
  generic function you already use still works on it
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
# a serial interval, censored and truncated
si = double_interval_censored(
  sequential(generation_time, incubation);
  upper = 15, interval = 1)

# and what comes back
IntervalCensored{Truncated{
  PrimaryCensored{Convolved{...}}}}
```

::: {.callout-important}
This works for delays today. A renewal process, an ARIMA latent
process and an ODE are not distributions, so there is no story yet for
the time series half of this deck, and none for the fitting layer,
which is what the probabilistic programming language was doing.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
The language was always meant to be backend agnostic. This is what
taking that seriously looks like.
:::

::: {.attribution}
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22, `main` checked 2026-08-10. A
`DynamicPPL` package extension exists on an unmerged branch, not on
`main`. Open issue `CensoredDistributions.jl#749` says the joint fit is
too slow, because reverse mode autodiff through `cdf(Convolved(...))`
costs too much per step. The delay side of this is written up in full at
